recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is recommended unless Patient Care later wants a specific reusable profile constraining Procedure.occurrenceDateTime precision for an implementation context.
issue_request: FHIR-16352 was a Published Patient Care change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking how to specify precise Procedure start/end times when a procedure is automatically started or stopped by a device. The resolution said not to use instant to distinguish device capture; profiles should constrain dateTime to precise UTC-with-timezone when needed, and Procedure.performed should explain that dateTime supports a range of precision.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit 2abadfb0e67fcff244d11e84699e185273719afa, whose subject includes "GF#16352 - add comments to Procedure.performed" and whose patch added the dateTime precision / UTC timestamp sentence to source/procedure/procedure-spreadsheet.xml. The current XML source inherited that comment through later source conversion.
additional_context: Procedure is active in source/fhir.ini and remains assigned to Patient Care. Later Published issue FHIR-20627 renamed Procedure.performed[x] to Procedure.occurrence[x] and added Timing while preserving the FHIR-16352 comment. Current Procedure source has no conflicting instant guidance, and community searches found no Zulip or Confluence record that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the current active Procedure.occurrence[x] comment already states that dateTime supports varying precision, including more precise UTC timestamps with timezone for procedures documented during an encounter.

related_jiras.note: Renamed Procedure.performed[x] to Procedure.occurrence[x] and added Timing, explaining why the current element name differs from the original FHIR-16352 request while preserving the same timing clarification.
A contemporaneous Appointment no-change issue discussed dateTime versus instant for exact times, but it concerned Appointment rather than Procedure and did not require a Procedure source change.
